items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Lee Rainey asked me to play for a dance with him... Lee Rainey came to my house and asked me if I would like to work at a road house with him... The other musicians that Lee engaged were Edgar Courance...

ctx.x: I did not care too much about the way Johnny Dunn played, but I did copy the way he played "I've Been Down So Long", because I was learning the trumpet and it was something to help me learn the horn better.

A month or so after I had come home, a drummer by the name of Lee Rainey asked me to play for a dance with him in a small town up state Ohio. Lee was an amateur drummer but he had played with Clarence Page at times. I accepted the engagement and had learnt the "Tin Roof Blues" well enough to make Lee compliment me on the way I played it, and we played it a few times that night.

A few nights later, there was a dance at the Sterling Hotel and the band was a pick up, one that was being lead by a trumpet player named Chet. He had played in Chicago for a long time and he was a good trumpet player. I never knew why he came back to Cincinnati. Actually he lived across the river in Covington but worked in Cincinnati most of the time.
